request: Charlotte to Atlanta on February 4th for the customer workshop. I did think about driving, it's about three hours forty-five each way and roughly 490 miles there and back, but I'd lose most of the day, so I'd rather fly. Cheapest economy please.

must_keep.quote: Air travel should be considered the last alternative after all other options to conduct business have been considered (i.e. Video/Telecommunications conferencing, e-mail, or telephone). If the destination is under four hours of driving time, consideration must be given to driving instead of flying.
must_keep.why: driving under four hours must be considered, not chosen

must_keep.quote: All airline tickets must be booked at the lowest available airfare as determined by Concur or the Travel Desk (subject to the parameters defined in this section).
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest available airfare

must_keep.quote: Our policy is that domestic air purchases are coach class, regardless of flight time, and booked via nonrefundable tickets.
must_keep.why: domestic trips are coach, whatever the flight time

distractors.quote: For travel where the round trip travel distance exceeds 500 miles (800 km), personal car mileage may not be reimbursed
distractors.why: a distance rule for personal-car mileage, not for flying

distractors.quote: Wi-Fi in flight (GOGO)-is reimbursable ONLY for flights over 1.5 hours.
distractors.why: a flight-length rule for Wi-Fi fees, not for the cabin

design_notes: The drive is under four hours, so driving 'must be considered' (lines 383-384); the traveller has considered it and flies, which the clause allows. The 500-mile personal-car rule (lines 664-665) is about mileage, not flying. The lowest available airfare.
